purpose: The example sentences that DESIGN-r2.md and DESIGN-r3.md use to illustrate detection rules, kept as test data apart from the design prose. Each text is verbatim from its source as it stood before this file was introduced; line breaks inside a text are those of the source.

examples.text: The Unruh temperature, which is state-independent, sets the calibration
examples.exercises: binding of the relative pronoun `which` in a comma-introduced copular relative clause to a subject-lexicon term in the five tokens before it

examples.text:
"coupling-degree minimization" → "minimization of the coupling degree", "minimizing the coupling
degree"
examples.exercises: derivation of the nominalized and gerund forms of a subject that is itself a nominalization
examples.expected: the anchor subject and both derived forms are members of the rule's subject equivalence set

examples.text:
"state-independent" ≡ "independent of the state" ≡ "the same / identical / unchanged in every
state" ≡ "insensitive to the state"
examples.exercises: predicate synonyms that state the same quantified content as the anchor predicate
examples.expected: every listed predicate form is a member of the rule's predicate equivalence set

examples.exercises: literal detection of the formula without the square
examples.expected: a unit containing the formula has a finding with code L (not PASS)

examples.exercises: literal rule whose subject is "the framework's answer"; the quoted opening of control P-KDEG-3
examples.expected: FAIL (the first r3 run passed it, the single first-run failure)

source.section: 7 Mechanisms added after the first measurements

examples.exercises: predicate stated without its subject in reach, the antecedent two sentences back (code P, strong cue)
examples.expected: FAIL (code P); lost by r3 before code P was added, caught by r2
